meta.description: The Fire and Emergency Services (F&ES) Flight operates 24/7/365 to provide rapid, comprehensive emergency response, including structural fire suppression, Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF), hazardous materials (HAZMAT) response, technical rescue, and emergency medical services (EMS). Personnel maintain constant combat and emergency readiness while performing daily vehicle maintenance, equipment testing, facility fire prevention inspections, and rigorous physical and tactical training. Operating in a highly dynamic, industrial, and high-hazard environment, this work center is dedicated to protecting life, property, and mission-critical assets across the installation.
meta.references: Foundational workplace safety and JSTO development requirements are mandated by DAFI 91-202 (The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program), DAFMAN 91-203 (Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire, and Health Standards), and federal OSHA standards under Title 29 CFR § 1910. Operational guidelines, training, and emergency response parameters are dictated by AFMAN 32-1007 (Fire and Emergency Services Flight Operations), alongside overarching DoD policy defined in DoDI 6055.06 and DoDM 6055.06, which ensure adherence to National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) professional qualifications. Furthermore, due to the high-hazard nature of firefighting and medical response, strict occupational health directives apply; these include DAFI 48-137 for the Respiratory Protection Program (governing SCBA use), AFI 48-127 for the Occupational Noise and Hearing Conservation Program, and 29 CFR § 1910.1030 to ensure compliance with Bloodborne Pathogens standards.
meta.jhaNotes: A comprehensive Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) must address diverse operational risks. Personnel face environmental hazards like seasonal heat and flooding, alongside facility-specific dangers such as faulty electrical equipment, wet floors, high noise, and poor air quality, which are mitigated through regular inspections and mandatory PPE. Highway operations introduce significant risks from managing large apparatus in high-speed traffic and adverse conditions, requiring strict adherence to vehicle placement and safety protocols. Furthermore, emergency medical responses present a primary hazard of exposure to contagious diseases and bloodborne pathogens. This risk is controlled by the mandatory use of specific PPE—including high-risk surgical gloves and eye protection—and adherence to stringent decontamination procedures.

meta.medicalFacility: The Hunters Medical Clinic (Bldg 1033) serves as the primary medical facility on Creech AFB, providing Flight Medicine, Family Health, and outpatient services during duty hours (Monday–Friday). On-base emergencies requiring immediate medical treatment are handled by calling 911 (or 702-404-0911 from a cell phone) to initiate a response from the clinic’s localized ambulance service. For acute or after-hours emergencies, patients are transported to the 24/7 Emergency Department at Mike O'Callaghan Military Medical Center on Nellis AFB or local civilian trauma facilities. Active-duty personnel requiring standard medical treatment must utilize scheduled appointments or the designated morning flight medicine sick call, and they must contact the Nurse Advice Line for off-base urgent care referrals to avoid unauthorized billing.
meta.evacuationRoute: According to the emergency procedures outlined in your JSTO, personnel will evacuate to designated assembly points, ensuring they evacuate all fire vehicles and apparatus from the bays only if it is safe to do so. For personnel in Building 1150, the muster point is the parking lot located to the west of the main entrance. For personnel in Building 85, the evacuation point is the theater parking lot (Bldg. 39). All individuals must remain at their designated assembly point until formally cleared to leave by Senior Fire Officer.
